standard_prerequisites.name: Ampness, very ampleness and Bertini type statements for the construction of the Chern classes

core_obligations: Define the Chern classes of a finite locally free module (proof lines 4135-4161): decompose the scheme into finitely many open and closed pieces over which the module has constant rank, use that the cohomology ring of the disjoint union is the product of the rings, and in the constant rank case define the Chern classes through the projective bundle and the displayed relation, with the total Chern class the sum of the individual classes.

Basic properties (proof lines 4163-4200): for an invertible module the total Chern class reduces to one plus the first Chern class; the Chern classes are central because the first Chern class of the twist of the projective bundle commutes with pullbacks of arbitrary classes; the construction is compatible with pullbacks because pulling back the defining relation along the morphism of projective bundles gives the defining relation for the pullback of the module.

Multiplicativity in short exact sequences (proof lines 4202-4262): for a short exact sequence with invertible submodule one uses that the projective bundle of the quotient is the zero scheme of a regular section of a twisted invertible module, so the defining relation pulls back to zero, and the axiom on zero schemes of regular sections converts this into the identity expressing multiplicativity; the general case is reduced to this one by induction on the rank, pulling back along the projective bundle of the dual to exhibit an invertible submodule.

Descend to K theory and prove uniqueness (proof lines 4264-4283): the multiplicativity in short exact sequences shows that sending a class to the total Chern class of a representative and extending multiplicatively is well defined on the Grothendieck group; uniqueness follows by induction on the rank, using the pullback to a projective bundle and the multiplicativity to reduce to modules of smaller rank.
proof_roadmap: Construct the Chern classes via projective bundles and check the elementary properties.
Prove multiplicativity in short exact sequences by induction on the rank.
Descend the construction to the Grothendieck group and prove uniqueness by induction.
difficulty_reason: The proposition proves that there is a unique rule assigning to every scheme of the category a total Chern class on the Grothendieck group of vector bundles valued in the cohomology ring, additive for sums, compatible with pullbacks and normalized on invertible modules (statement lines 4124-4139). The proof (proof lines 4140-4283) constructs the Chern classes through projective bundles, verifies centrality and pullback compatibility, proves multiplicativity in short exact sequences by induction on the rank, descends to the Grothendieck group, and proves uniqueness. H3: a long construction with an induction and a uniqueness argument, written out in full.
